_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG15-FG20_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — pulled from the client's Drive on 2026-09-16. FG-20 'Performance & Volume' holds 5 cases: TC-PERF-001, -002, -003, -004, -007. All 5 are implemented and all 5 are BLOCKED — by their own instruction.
_why_all_five_block: Every case says the same thing in its preconditions: 'Novobi has given you the timings for the same steps on the old system. Without them this case cannot be judged — record it as Blocked rather than guessing.' There is no baseline on file, so no verdict is available and inventing a threshold would be exactly the guessing the workbook forbids. What every case DOES do is measure the v19 side first — three runs per step, middle value kept, the workbook's own method — and export it as a CSV artifact. The day Novobi supplies the v15 numbers they go into reports/data/fg20_baseline.json (see fg20_baseline.json.example) and these same tests start judging at the workbook's 1.5x tolerance with no change to any of them.
_what_is_being_timed: The workbook times a stopwatch from clicking a menu to the rows finishing: server PLUS transport PLUS render. This suite times the server call the list view actually issues — web_search_read, the same one the browser sends, reading the columns the view itself declares rather than a convenient subset. So these are query times, not paint times. The difference cuts both ways and is stated in every case's log: a server number cannot clear a screen that is slow for rendering reasons (and FG-15 showed how much this stack leans on custom widgets), but it is reproducible where a stopwatch is not, and a query that takes thirty seconds cannot be rescued by any front-end work. If Novobi's v15 figures were taken with a stopwatch, the two are not the same measurement — the example baseline file says so at the top.
_a_false_green_that_was_closed: judge_or_block originally treated any non-empty baseline object as usable. A skeleton file with the step labels present and their values left null would have made it truthy, the comparison loop would have skipped every step, and the case would have gone GREEN having compared nothing — the worst possible outcome for a case whose entire subject is a comparison. Only numeric, positive entries now count, and any measured step with no baseline beside it is reported as an uncompared gap and fails the coverage check.

_findings.BC-FG20-001: A bulk write over 1,000 products TOOK THE INSTANCE DOWN. An earlier revision of TC-PERF-004 measured the wizard's write by writing each product's existing taxes back onto itself — the same ORM path, no data change. That produced roughly 47,000 attachment reads in two minutes (odoo19 log, 11:51-11:53) and the Odoo process restarted at the end of the burst; the run died with 'Connection refused'. Nothing was damaged: only 15 product templates carried a new write_date afterwards and all 95,020 tax links were untouched. But a tax write on a product cascading into ~47 attachment reads EACH is precisely what TC-PERF-004 exists to find. On this instance every one of those reads raises FileNotFoundError because the restore carries no filestore (TC-SMK-014); on a system with one they would succeed, and still be ~47,000 file opens for 1,000 writes. Worth Novobi's attention independently of any baseline.
_findings.OBS-FG20-001: Volumes measured on this database: 67,181 active products (69,536 including archived, against the 69,201 the workbook states), 43,190 orders (43,117 stated), 110,051 journal entries (109,218 stated), 329,539 journal items, 6,866,084 sync-log rows. Every list case checks its own volume within 5% of the stated figure, counting archived records — a product list shows ACTIVE rows and the workbook's production figure counts everything, so comparing the wrong one would manufacture a shortfall that is not there.
_findings.OBS-FG20-002: The five accounting reports TC-PERF-003 names all exist, but the report engine is not driven from here: its entry point takes a fully-built options dict the web client composes, so timing it over RPC would measure a different thing and call it the same name. The invoice list IS the same call the screen makes, so those two numbers are comparable; the report timings are named as residual manual instead of being approximated.

TC-PERF-001.reason: BLOCKED on the baseline; the v19 side is measured. Times the product list at default width and at 500 rows, a name search on the three fields the search bar really covers (name, internal reference, barcode — NOT artist, as the workbook notes), a group by category and the expansion of the largest group. Volume checked against the stated 69,201.

TC-PERF-002.reason: BLOCKED on the baseline; the v19 side is measured. Times the order list at both widths, the Cancelled filter, and grouping by Shipping Status and by Store. It also answers one thing that needs no baseline at all and asserts it: the Shipping Status buckets add up to the list total.

TC-PERF-003.reason: BLOCKED on the baseline AND on the agreed date range. The invoice list is timed at both widths and the journal-entry volume checked; the five reports are confirmed to exist but are named as residual manual for the reason in OBS-FG20-002. Step 8's layout comparison needs both systems open.

TC-PERF-004.reason: BLOCKED on the baseline. Selects exactly 1,000 products as steps 1-2 require, confirms the wizard and its Customer Taxes field, times the READ of those 1,000 products' taxes, and records their full tax state so a real run's partial completion would be visible. The WRITE is deliberately not made — see BC-FG20-001. The workbook's own precondition offers the alternative: 'or the test system is a throwaway copy', where the literal steps are safe and should be run once.

TC-PERF-007.reason: BLOCKED on the baseline and on Novobi's kept-row figures from the clear-out. Times all three log types for one store — opening with the default Draft/Failed/Unresolved chips, with them cleared, at 500 rows, and grouped by Status — and records the per-store counts the workbook says to compare against what the clear-out kept. Those counts are far smaller than the 6.87M whole-table figure, which the workbook says is expected because no screen shows the whole table.
